title: Like-minded sources on Facebook are prevalent but not polarizing
screen_reason: Although the paper's aim is echo chambers and polarization, it reports a behavioural share of Facebook Feed exposures coming from 'misinformation repeat offenders' (sources Facebook identifies as repeatedly posting misinformation): the average proportion of exposures was 0.76% in the control group. That is an EXPOSURE share with a behavioural denominator (all Feed content views).

estimates.measure_type: % of Facebook Feed content exposures that came from misinformation repeat-offender sources (untreated control group)
estimates.value_raw: 'the average proportion of exposures decreased ... from 0.76% to 0.55% for content from misinformation repeat offenders' (0.76% = control group, 0.55% = treatment group)
estimates.denominator: All Facebook Feed content views of control-group participants during the 3-month experiment (the average control participant had 267 content views on a typical day); participants were consenting US adult Facebook users, n = 23,377 randomized to treatment or control with equal probability
estimates.definition: Content whose source is identified by Facebook as repeatedly posting misinformation ('misinformation repeat offenders'), as a proportion of all content views in the participant's Feed
estimates.misinfo_def: content from misinformation repeat offenders (sources identified by Facebook as repeatedly posting misinformation)
estimates.n: Feed content exposures of the control group (about 11,700 of the 23,377 randomized US adult Facebook users; ~267 views per participant per day)
estimates.source_quote: Substantively, the average proportion of exposures decreased from 0.034% to 0.030% for content with slur words (a reduction of 0.01 views per day on average), from 3.15% to 2.81% for uncivil content (a reduction of 1.24 views per day on average), and from 0.76% to 0.55% for content from misinformation repeat offenders (a reduction of 0.62 views per day on average).
estimates.page_loc: Results, 'Experiment reducing like-minded source exposure', Nature vol. 620, p. 141
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Meta's internal 'misinformation repeat offender' designation — sources identified by Facebook as repeatedly posting misinformation. The measurement details are deferred to Supplementary Information section 1.3, which is not part of this text, so the rating procedure (third-party fact-check driven) cannot be verified from the paper text.
estimates.moderator_quote: content from misinformation repeat offenders (sources identified by Facebook as repeatedly posting misinformation) ... Civic and news content make up a relatively small share of what people see on Facebook, however (medians of 6.9% and 6.7%, respectively)
estimates.notes: The control-group value is taken as the representative descriptive point; the treatment arm (0.55%) is the same measure after an intervention that downranked like-minded sources, so it is not a separate descriptive estimate and no second row was created. denom_scope=all_media because the denominator is ALL Feed content views, not a news or political subset (civic content is a median 6.9% of what users see). breadth is blank because the classification is source-level (a platform repeat-offender list), not an item-level veracity judgement. topic coded general_news because the repeat-offender designation is not topic-restricted, even though the study runs over the 2020 US election.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: the like-minded / cross-cutting exposure shares (50.4%, 14.7%, 53.7% etc.) and the uncivil-content and slur-word shares, which are not misinformation measures; all treatment effects, which are reported in standard deviations only; belief in false claims (a belief outcome, excluded by protocol); engagement with misinformation repeat offenders, reported only as s.d. effects with no share. Extended Data Table 3 and the Supplementary Tables that would give the exact control-group denominators are not in this text.

rob.design: Population-level platform logs for all US adult monthly active Facebook users plus a preregistered 3-month field experiment (n = 23,377 consenting users, block-randomized with equal probability, participants blind); exposure measured from on-platform behavioural data; source political leaning and 'misinformation repeat offender' status assigned by internal Facebook classifiers/designations; academic authors held control rights and Meta could not block publication; analysis preregistered (osf.io/3sjy2).
rob.item6_quote: content from misinformation repeat offenders (sources identified by Facebook as repeatedly posting misinformation)
rob.item10_quote: Substantively, the average proportion of exposures decreased ... from 0.76% to 0.55% for content from misinformation repeat offenders (a reduction of 0.62 views per day on average).
